key_insight: A ternary-solvent growth strategy produces large-area hybrid perovskite monolayers, enabling lithography-free optoelectronic devices with ultra-low static power.
engineering_relevance: Large isolated flakes support solvent-free shadow-mask contacts, avoiding solvent-induced lithography damage while reducing standby power.
method: Combine alcohol cosolvents with an amine additive to suppress out-of-plane stacking.
Tune precursor solvation and annealing transport to promote lateral growth.
Fabricate planar devices on isolated ultrathin perovskite channels using physical shadow masks.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports monolayer areas exceeding 1,000 µm² and ultrathin (PEA)₂PbI₄ devices consuming approximately 0.2 pW at 5 V—250-fold below drop-cast films—with a light-to-dark current ratio of 430.
watch_item: The abstract does not establish wafer-scale uniformity, long-term device stability, or solar-cell performance; the demonstrated application is low-static-power optoelectronics, not AI or photovoltaics.
paper_title: Universal Synthesis of Large-Area Hybrid Perovskite Monolayers Enabling Lithography-Free, Low-Static-Power Optoelectronics
